title: About
text:
My academic path has taken me from Wisconsin to Singapore, Chicago, and Seattle, combining training in economics, mathematics, social science, and marketing analytics.
Before starting my PhD, I completed internships spanning financial analysis, market research and consulting, and technology.

Outside Research


Outside of research, I am a cat mom, a dancer, and an enthusiastic home cook. I am also a foodie who loves exploring local coffee roasters and trying new restaurants.
I am currently learning tennis, though reaching 3.0 may still be a few hundred million lessons away.

I am a third-year PhD student in Economics at the University of Washington. My research is in development economics, applied microeconomics, and econometrics. I study household decision-making, fertility, saving and consumption, and the long-run effects of environmental shocks.





Research design in progress.
I am developing an experiment that studies whether feedback on consumption-forecast errors helps initially naive individuals become more sophisticated about their future spending, and whether greater sophistication affects saving and consumption smoothing.



Preliminary analysis in progress.
I study how fertility constraints affect women’s labor supply, economic outcomes, and bargaining power within households.



Preliminary analysis in progress.
I study how exposure to major floods at different stages of life affects long-run health.
